prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (non-exhaustive)

Fiscal and tax
- Fund priorities by ending net EU contributions, reducing overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI over three years, cancelling HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system, and cutting central government and quango costs.
- Invest over the parliament: NHS (+£12bn), social care (+£5.2bn), defence (to ≥2% of GDP), mental health and dementia (+£1.5bn), carers (+£572/year), police/prisons/border staff (+6,000).
- Tax changes: raise personal allowance to at least £13,000; remove income tax from minimum wage; new 30% band between £43,500–£55,000; raise 40% threshold to £55,000; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowance for couples to £1,500; zero-rate VAT on listed-building repairs and sanitary products; tackle multinational profit shifting.

Immigration
- Leave the EU to regain border control; five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; Australian-style points system; annual cap of 50,000 highly skilled work visas; create a Migration Control Commission.
- Count every entrant/exiter; expand Border Agency by 2,500; no amnesty for illegal immigrants; faster asylum decisions.
- Five years of tax/NI before access to most benefits and non-urgent NHS; require medical insurance for visitors/workers; deport foreign criminals; revise family and citizenship rules.

Health and social care
- Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP presence in A&E pilots; expand psychiatric liaison; increase dementia research/treatment.
- Free hospital parking; tighten cost recovery from ineligible patients; require insurance for non-residents.
- Replace Monitor and CQC with locally elected professional county health boards; “licence to manage” for NHS managers; end PFI use; seek changes to EU rules affecting training/trials.
- Restore social care funding to 2010 levels (+£1.2bn/year); integrate health and social care under the NHS; dignity code; end 15‑minute home visits; improve pay/practices for home-care workers.

Welfare, pensions, family
- Keep housing benefit for under‑25s; scrap “bedroom tax”; allow direct rent payment to landlords; limit child benefit to two children for new claims; stop payments for children abroad; five-year benefit wait for new migrants.
- Replace disability assessments with GP/specialist-led model; fund advisers in foodbanks.
- Flexible state pension window; expand free pensions guidance; ban pension cold-calling; restore war widows’ pensions for life.
- Childcare: keep 15 free hours; broaden voucher use to approved informal carers; require wraparound care 8am–6pm in primaries; expand places via planning.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; cut workload and class sizes over time; scrap performance-related pay.
- Support grammar, vocational and technical routes; later transfer tests; strengthen apprenticeships; GCSE/AS reforms; first-aid in PSHE.
- Reopen/expand special schools; streamline Ofsted onto teaching/wellbeing; waive tuition fees for UK STEMM/Medicine graduates who work and pay tax in the UK for five years.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield with a national register, remediation support and stamp duty relief on first sales up to £250k; bring empty homes back into use; aim for 1m brownfield homes by 2025.
- National Homeless Register; restrict new access to social housing to those resident and contributing for five years.
- Reinforce green belt; empower local referenda on major developments; enable inheritable mortgages; no mansion tax.

Transport and energy
- Cancel HS2; consider South East capacity after the Davies report; support reopening Manston.
- Limit speed cameras to safety use; phase out tolls; oppose road pricing/eCall; scrap DCPC; double HGV levy for foreign trucks; VED exemption for vehicles >25 years.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; remove green levies/ETS; back a diverse energy mix; end subsidies for new onshore wind/solar, retain hydro; support shale with safeguards and a sovereign wealth fund; sustain coal with CCS.

Jobs, business, farming, fishing
- Prioritise resident workers; enforce minimum wage; regulate zero‑hours abuses.
- 20% business rates relief up to £50k rateable value; clamp down on late payments via HMRC fines; pilot trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; simplify SME public procurement.
- New Single Farm Payment (capped), support for dairy and hill farms; clearer food labelling; tougher animal welfare; CCTV in abattoirs; ban live exports for slaughter.
- Leave the Common Fisheries Policy; 12‑mile UK-only and 200‑mile UK-controlled zones; rebuild stocks, protect inshore fleet and sea angling; permit foreign access only when sustainable.

Crime, governance, culture, defence, aid, Brexit
- Add frontline police/prison/border staff; domestic Bill of Rights; review offences/sentencing; reduce constabulary duplication; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment; cut FOBT stakes to £2; deport foreign prisoners.
- Citizens’ initiative referendums; real recall; open primaries; select committee confirmation and spending veto powers; proportional voting with constituency link; tighten postal voting.
- Promote English (plus Welsh/Gaelic) in official use; protect free speech within the law; require transparency around faith-based tribunals; mandatory FGM reporting/training; add St George’s/St David’s Day bank holidays.
- Defence: spend ≥2% of GDP, rising by ~£4bn by 2020; retain nuclear deterrent; rebuild capabilities; create a Director of National Intelligence; no EU army; remove income tax on operational duty.
- Overseas aid: reduce to 0.2% GNI, focus on emergencies, health, water/sanitation; close DFID and merge functions into the Foreign Office.
- Hold an in/out referendum; prefer Article 50 process; seek EU free-trade access and targeted cooperation; create a Post‑EU Secretariat; reoccupy the UK’s WTO seat and negotiate global deals.
